title: Java native deserialization gadget assessment
summary: Identify whether native Java serialization accepts untrusted bytes and whether classpath gadgets can turn object reconstruction into code execution.
preconditions: The tester is authorized to submit a controlled serialized object to an isolated lab.
A Java endpoint or protocol accepts untrusted serialized data.
verification_method: Confirm the endpoint decodes a known harmless serialized object and changes behavior.
Use a callback-only gadget chain to prove deserialization before attempting any file or command impact.
Compare behavior with serialization filters enabled and disabled.
known_failures: A content type or magic-byte check can occur before deserialization.
The server may use JSON or another format despite a Java stack.
Missing library versions or serialization filters can make a known chain unusable.
steps: Locate binary bodies, cookies, view state, RMI, JMX, or message payloads that begin with Java serialization magic bytes.
Decode a trusted sample and confirm the object format.
Send a minimal object that should be accepted by the target class and observe the response.
Use an out-of-band harmless callback chain only in an authorized lab to prove code path execution.
Record the exact library versions and filter configuration needed for reproduction.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP Top 10 2017 A8: Insecure Deserialization; CWE-502
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: Session fixation before and after authentication
summary: Test whether an attacker-chosen session identifier remains valid after login instead of being rotated.
preconditions: The tester can control a session cookie in an authorized browser session.
verification_method: Capture the session identifier before login and compare it after successful authentication.
Repeat with an attacker-supplied valid identifier in the lab and verify whether it remains authorized.
Check logout and privilege-change flows for session rotation.
known_failures: The framework may rotate identifiers while preserving another token or remember-me cookie.
A signed or encrypted session may reject an arbitrary externally chosen value.
Multi-device authentication can create multiple valid identifiers.
steps: Obtain a pre-authentication session and record its identifier and attributes.
Authenticate in the same session and compare the identifier and authorization state.
In a separate lab account, supply a controlled pre-login identifier and observe whether it becomes authenticated.
Inspect response Set-Cookie headers and server-side session metadata at each transition.
Verify that logout invalidates both the pre-login and post-login identifiers.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Session Fixation; CWE-384
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: Default credential and weak account policy assessment
summary: Test authorized lab systems for unchanged default accounts, exposed setup paths, and account-state logic that permits unintended access.
preconditions: The tester is authorized to use known lab credentials and account recovery paths.
Rate limits and lockout controls are understood before testing.
verification_method: Confirm whether a default account is enabled using documentation-backed credentials only in the lab.
Compare access with a normal low-privilege user and inspect the resulting session role.
Verify that setup or recovery paths cannot be reused after initialization.
known_failures: Default credentials may be rejected but another privileged API key remains valid.
Account lockout can make repeated testing disruptive.
UI login failure may differ from an API-level authentication result.
steps: Inventory authentication endpoints, setup paths, and administrative roles from authorized documentation.
Check vendor documentation for default accounts and whether deployment instructions require rotation.
Perform a single controlled login attempt with a documented lab credential and record the resulting role.
Test whether password reset or first-run setup exposes a separate account takeover path.
Report any default account together with the configuration and rotation requirement.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Weak Authentication; CWE-1392
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: JWT alg none acceptance probe
summary: Test whether a verifier accepts an unsigned JWT or fails to pin the expected signing algorithm.
preconditions: The tester can obtain and modify a JWT in the authorized lab.
The JWT is used by an endpoint with a known unauthenticated baseline.
verification_method: Compare a valid signed token with an unsigned token whose claims and casing are controlled.
Confirm the server accepts the modified payload claim through an authenticated endpoint.
Verify that strict algorithm allowlisting rejects the same token after configuration change.
known_failures: Modern JWT libraries reject none by default.
The endpoint may require a token that fails signature checks before authorization logic.
Some proxies normalize or strip the trailing segment.
steps: Decode a valid JWT and record header, claims, issuer, audience, and expiration.
Create a controlled unsigned variant with the same claims and an explicit alg value of none.
Send the original and modified tokens to the same endpoint and compare authorization state.
Test uppercase and lowercase algorithm spellings only if library behavior makes them relevant.
Avoid changing privileged claims until the algorithm acceptance signal is proven.

provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: JWT symmetric and asymmetric key confusion assessment
summary: Assess whether a verifier accepts an unexpected algorithm and misuses an asymmetric public key as an HMAC secret.
preconditions: The tester can retrieve or infer the public verification key in an authorized lab.
The service accepts JWTs signed with multiple algorithm families.
verification_method: Compare JWT headers and validate whether the server enforces a fixed allowed algorithm.
Use a controlled test key and benign claims to test cross-family verification behavior.
Confirm strict key-usage and algorithm checks after remediation.
known_failures: The verifier may use separate endpoints or keys for each algorithm.
Key encoding differences can prevent reproducing the exact HMAC input.
Token revocation or application state can reject otherwise valid forged claims.
steps: Decode several valid tokens and record declared algorithm, kid, issuer, and key source.
Retrieve the public verification key through its documented endpoint or configuration.
In a lab, create a token with a different algorithm family and a minimally changed benign claim.
Send the token to a read-only endpoint and compare acceptance with a valid signed token.
Document exact key bytes, algorithm allowlist, and library version required for reproduction.

provenance.source_ref: PortSwigger Web Security Academy: JWT attacks; CWE-347
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: IDOR object reference authorization test
summary: Test whether changing an object identifier crosses an authorization boundary while using a valid low-privilege session.
preconditions: Two controlled lab accounts or objects exist.
The tester is authorized to access only the test objects.
verification_method: Request account A's object with account B's session and compare with the owner's response.
Use both sequential IDs and non-sequential IDs to test object ownership rather than guessability.
Confirm denial at the server API layer, not only in the UI.
known_failures: A 404, 403, or empty response can already indicate correct authorization.
The object may be public or intentionally shared, making disclosure non-sensitive.
Frontend hiding of controls does not prove API authorization.
steps: Create two controlled records owned by different test identities.
Capture authenticated read and update requests for each record.
Replay account A's request with account B's session while changing only the object identifier.
Compare status, body, side effects, and whether an audit event is generated.
Test read, update, and delete separately because authorization checks often differ.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Insecure Direct Object References; CWE-639
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.

title: CSRF on a state-changing endpoint
summary: Determine whether a browser-confused authenticated request can change state without an unpredictable token or strict origin enforcement.
preconditions: The tester has a controlled authenticated session and account.
The state change is reversible or uses a disposable lab object.
verification_method: Replay a valid state-changing request after removing token fields and changing the Origin or Referer.
Host a controlled cross-origin form in the lab and observe whether the state change occurs.
Confirm SameSite cookie behavior and server-side token validation separately.
known_failures: SameSite=Lax or Strict cookies can block the cross-site request.
A custom header requirement can prevent simple form-based CSRF.
JSON endpoints may reject form content types but still accept a CSRF-able method.
steps: Identify a reversible state change such as a profile note or test setting.
Capture the legitimate request, including cookies, token fields, content type, and origin headers.
Replay without the token and with a controlled cross-origin Origin header.
If rejected, test alternate methods and encodings only within the authorized scope.
Prove the state changed by reading it back and restore the original value.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Cross Site Request Forgery; CWE-352
provenance.notes: Human-curated paraphrase; no exact deep URL embedded.
